claim: C16 — ternary quantization of question-map embeddings; C17 — calibrated mass vs ordinal levels
registration: experiments/pre_registration_e_q22.json + AM1 (the NO-NEIGHBOR strict scoring rule, appended after the eval run and BEFORE hypothesis sealing)

task.arms: S score-continuous (E-Q21 sealed rows, zero new calls) / N noul-continuous (23 r24 calls) / TS score-ternary / TN noul-ternary (median-centered {-1,0,+1}, MAD 0.5)

scoring.rule: AM1: strict governs (NO-NEIGHBOR = miss, denominator 20); lenient = as-measured denominator

ternarization.rule: +1 if x > m+0.5*MAD; -1 if x < m-0.5*MAD; else 0 (m/MAD per axis over the arm's 20 corpus vectors)

verdict: E-Q22 VERDICT (the axis-calibration x ternary-quantization factorial — C16/C17, AM1 strict scoring): H1 LIVES — C17 LIVES: the NOUL-calibrated arm retrieves at 0.8 top-1 versus the ordinal score arm's 0.7 (both arms re-upserted and re-queried LIVE this lane — the S arm's 0.70 replicates E-Q21 through a fresh changeset, itself a stability receipt; the same 8 axis CONCEPTS, only the question TYPE changed). The jev-lattice calibration confound is real and fixable: typing the axes as calibrated mass gains a record, widens the separation margin (same-minus-cross 0.2565 vs 0.2153), and stabilizes the vectors ~10x (F5: 24/24 axes within 0.10, max delta 0.03). H2 DIES: the ternary survival clause fails on the noul side — TS 0.6 retains 0.8571 of S (within the 0.85 clause), but TN 0.55 retains only 0.6875 of N (0.25 absolute drop vs the 0.15 registered tolerance; lenient cross-check 0.6471 vs required 0.65 — fails by 0.003 there, by 0.10 strict: the verdict is identical under both scorings). H3 LIVES: both ternary arms clear the baselines decisively (TS 0.6 and TN 0.55 vs majority 0.25 and permutation null 0.2122) — the 16-bit ternary code carries the family signal at 2.4-2.2x the majority baseline. H4 DIES: ternarization INVERTS the calibration effect ((TN - TS) = -0.05 vs (N - S) = 0.1): calibration and quantization are SUBSTITUTES, not complements — the ordinal arm's mid-range spread survives median-centering better than the noul arm's saturated near-0/1 mass (noul saturation concentrates records at the code corners where intra-family resolution is lost). C16 (ternary at 16x compression) DIES with the honest narrowing: the code retains signal far above baselines with ZERO collisions (20 distinct codes, 1.5383/1.5198 bits/axis entropy — P4 HIT), but the strict retention clause fails on the noul side; C17 (calibrated mass beats ordinal levels) LIVES at 0.8 vs 0.7. The consumer law: for RETRIEVAL use the noul arm continuous (0.80, the new best single-jev configuration); for COMPRESSION use the score arm ternary (0.60 at 16 bits, 86% retention); never buy both — the noul-ternary combination is the worst of the four arms' retention ratios.
